payload.headline: Amazon slips 1.21% to 252.29; cash burn keeps us waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon keeps growing and its margins are improving, but it is spending more cash than it brings in, and the price already sits near the top of its usual value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price stays in a downtrend between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Buy at 238.65; small buy at 245.59 only after better cash flow; no buying above 265.96

payload.happening: Amazon closed at 252.29, down 1.21% on the day. The stock is in a downtrend. It trades below its 20-day average of 257.7 and its 50-day average of 255.15, but still above its 200-day average of 245.59. Amazon was reported to be buying Decart to help close its AI-chip gap with Nvidia, and the FAA was reported to be probing a delivery-drone accident. The next earnings report is due 2027-02-04.
payload.business: Sales are still growing, but more slowly. Quarterly sales rose 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the profit kept from each dollar of sales before interest and tax, improved to 13.09% from 11.02%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and paying for new buildings and equipment, was -46.9B over the last 12 months, against 10.6B a year earlier. Debt exceeds cash by 66.7B. Even so, 114.2B of liquidity (cash plus credit it can draw on) means there is no near-term funding risk. The filings also flag two things: unpaid customer bills grew 61% while sales grew 12%, and the 13% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%. Today's news changes little in the business. The reported Decart deal is a strategic bet on AI chips that could matter over the long run, but it does not change current demand or margins. The reported FAA drone probe is a regulatory and sentiment issue, not a hit to earnings. The Apple TV discount is minor. What is at risk is how much cash Amazon generates and how long its margin stays at the peak. Demand itself is not at risk: sales over the last 12 months reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value, a method that values a company by its future cash, because free cash flow is negative. That leaves the company's own price-to-sales history. Price-to-sales is the stock price divided by sales per share. Over 5 years, that history gives a fair-value range of 187.93 to 265.96, with a middle of 238.65. At 252.29 the stock is above the middle and below the top. Its price-to-sales of 3.4 sits at the 67th percentile of its own 5-year history, which means it has been cheaper about two-thirds of the time. Against peers it looks cheap: the peer median is 6.4, and on a growth-adjusted basis it trades at 0.62 of what peers trade at. The stock costs 20.5 times trailing earnings and 19.7 times this year's expected earnings. On next year's expected earnings the multiple rises to 23.6, because analysts expect earnings per share to fall from 12.8 to 10.67. The filings estimate that the price needs about 33% yearly growth, while the company delivered 13% a year over the last 3 years. Most of the gap between methods comes from one choice: whether Amazon should be valued against its own past or against its peers.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.4.

bull: Price-to-sales of 3.4 is well below the peer median of 6.4, and growth-adjusted value is 0.62 of peers.
Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now keeps more profit.
Sales over the last 12 months grew to 797.5B from 691.3B, and analysts expect 959.6B next year.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from 10.6B, and debt exceeds cash by 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, and unpaid customer bills grew 61%.
Analysts expect earnings per share to fall from 12.8 this year to 10.67 next year, which lifts the forward multiple to 23.6.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history value range, inside the 232.99–238.97 support zone (a price area where buyers have stepped in before). This is the main buy level.
The 200-day average, inside the strong 244.3–249.71 support zone (9 touches). A small first buy here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
The top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: At 252.29 the price is above the 238.65 middle of its value range, while the cash burn and slowing growth are unresolved. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend and sits in the 251.93–257.04 zone. Support at 244.3–249.71 and resistance at 258.08–263.7 are both within one typical day's move: the average true range, or typical daily move, is 9.99. No trade unless the price pulls back into 244.3–249.71 and holds there, or closes above 263.7.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-04 earnings report is the next test. Options expiring 2027-02-19, after that report, price in a move of about 15.5%, against 8.1% for the 2026-12-18 expiry. Next-quarter earnings estimates were cut 2.6% in the last 30 days, so any buy before the report should start at 238.65, not higher.

change_mind: Free cash flow in the next filing better than -46.9B, with quarterly sales growth back above 16.61%, would support buying at 245.59 instead of waiting for 238.65.
A close above 263.7, the top of the first resistance zone, would end the downtrend's lower-highs pattern and reopen a swing entry.
A close below 232.99, the bottom of the lower support zone, would cancel the 238.65 buy level and point toward the 187.93 low of the value range.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; today's 1.21% drop to 252.29 kept the price above the 238.65 buy level, and free cash flow is still -46.9B.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
